proposed_from.topic: K1 prove stable basin-mixed normality for bounded adaptive IPW-Z scores under a finite tail attractor and uniform attraction modulus. K2 prove realized-QV studentization uniformly pivotal. K3 prove a deterministic sandwich valid for a contrast at every nominal level iff its variance is basin-invariant. K4 prove validity for all contrasts iff V_J is deterministic. Include the Guo-Xu two-basin witness and HeartSteps consumer. PRESOLVE EVIDENCE REQUIRING VERIFICATION: Conditional predictable QV convergence Q_T/T to V_J gives the martingale stable-limit spine. Bounded scores support uniform Lindeberg, and realized minus predictable QV should be negligible, so same-path studentization removes the mixture. Identifiability of centered Gaussian scale mixtures yields necessity at every nominal level; one-level accidental coverage is excluded. Positive basin masses, eigenvalue bounds, attraction tails, and a Cesaro policy-error modulus make the class falsifiable. Separatrix uniformity remains unchecked. Equal scalar variances with unequal covariance matrices verify why contrastwise and matrixwise statements must remain distinct here. UNRESOLVED BOTTLENECK: Convert the attraction and Cesaro assumptions into one uniform triangular-array modulus sufficient for stable convergence, inverse-QV control, and matching near-separatrix bounds in the exact recursion. EARLY KILL TEST: Analyze and simulate the no-intercept recursion from states approaching the basin boundary. Pivot to margin-restricted inference if attraction tails are not uniform; stop if realized-QV t-statistics fail in either attained basin.
proposed_from.novelty_justification: The field-tier advance is the conditional finite-attractor theorem bundle: a basin-stable causal IPW-Z finite Gaussian mixture, uniformly feasible finite-sample-defined same-path realized-QV studentization, and exact contrastwise and matrixwise deterministic-sandwich iff boundaries. Theorem 2 strictly tightens Saco's pointwise realized-QV result on the stated conditional class. Guo--Xu, Shen and coauthors, Han, Leiner--Dunn--Ramdas, Borkar, and the remaining cited work supply motivation, ingredients, orthogonal regimes, or informed-by comparisons rather than a second strict comparator chain. The absence of two direct strict comparators caps the proposal at field tier, which is the requested floor and achieved target; no flagship novelty is claimed. The common basin-covariance lower bound and \(e_T=T^{-1/2}+r_T+\delta_T\) are proposal-specific class restrictions rather than conditions attributed to Saco or Mourrat; the covariance and Jacobian upper bounds are derived from existing score, overlap, and derivative envelopes. The bounded witness is non-novel, and finite projected tail dynamics plus relative-basin-interior attraction for the augmented bounded Rademacher Guo--Xu chain remain an open dynamics question rather than an assumed class-membership or inference result.

proposed_from.literature_map: The anchor scan covered each paper's motivation and terminal discussion together with the load-bearing theorem or proof construction. Guo--Xu's positive theorem uses scaled inverse-propensity convergence to obtain a deterministic Gaussian sandwich, whereas Section 3.1 gives only simulation evidence for two self-reinforcing clipped-LinUCB modes. Saco's main theorem already establishes pointwise realized-QV studentization by proving realized-to-predictable variance convergence and then invoking a self-normalized martingale CLT. Shen and coauthors obtain normal and efficient inference from deterministic target-specific directional QV. Leiner, Dunn, and Ramdas instead estimate time-varying covariance predictably and rescale the score. Borkar's Theorem 3.1 controls lock-in conditional on entry into an attraction set, and its conclusion leaves global and boundary-uniform control unresolved. Mourrat quantifies bounded-martingale Gaussian approximation through predictable-QV error but normalizes toward a deterministic variance. Teicher identifies finite normal mixtures, while Andrews and Mallows supply the normal-scale-mixture representation. Qian and coauthors define causal excursion effects and the HeartSteps analysis, and Zhang--Janson--Murphy supply the closest pooled adaptive Z-estimation decomposition under fixed within-user horizon. The exact occupied target is the generic pointwise realized-QV pivot; the unoccupied intersection is uniform finite-attractor verification, stable basin mixing, and the every-level deterministic-sandwich converse.
